pr.title: Verify that allocations output by GVN are sufficiently aligned.
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The historical regression (PR #127399, issue #127396) is not a runtime-value bug: it is a codegen ICE (`assertion failed: alloc_align >= layout.align.abi`). GVN propagating `ConstValue::Indirect` into an under-aligned `GlobalAlloc::Memory` changes only how the constant is represented, not the bits produced by the program. The test `misaligned-constant-gvn.rs` is `//@ build-pass` and prints the same transmuted value (`None::<u32>` as `u64` = 0) before and after the fix. A faithful Rust model of the wrong transformation would load a `u64` (align 8) from an allocation that is only 4-aligned; under Miri that is a misaligned-access UB diagnostic, not a defined differing value, while `read_unaligned` yields identical bits. Modeling the compiler invariant itself (e.g. returning whether `alloc.align >= layout.align`) would encode compiler internals rather than the program's historical semantics, and observing address alignment is explicitly disallowed. Therefore no source-grounded pair exists whose original and historically-wrong functions both have defined Miri executions that produce differing numeric/boolean/character values; the defect is a compile-time alignment invariant violation, not an observable semantic rewrite.

analysis.summary: GVN's `op_to_prop_const` propagated a pointer into a global allocation as `ConstValue::Indirect` whenever the allocation was `GlobalAlloc::Memory`, without checking the allocation's alignment against the operand layout's ABI alignment. For transmutes that reinterpret a smaller-aligned value as a larger-aligned type, the resulting indirect constant had insufficient alignment and later ICE'd in codegen (`assertion failed: alloc_align >= layout.align.abi`). The fix only uses `Indirect` when `alloc.inner().align >= op.layout.align.abi`, otherwise falling through to copying the value into a properly aligned temporary.
analysis.originalLogic: In `op_to_prop_const`, after `intern_const_alloc_for_constprop(ecx, alloc_id).ok()?;`, the original code was: `if matches!(ecx.tcx.global_alloc(alloc_id), GlobalAlloc::Memory(_)) {` then returned `Some(ConstValue::Indirect { alloc_id, offset })`. Thus any global memory allocation was propagated as an indirect constant, regardless of the operand layout's required alignment.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation: GVN propagates a pointer/projection into a `GlobalAlloc::Memory` allocation as `ConstValue::Indirect { alloc_id, offset }` even when `alloc.inner().align < op.layout.align.abi`. This represents the operand as a reference to the underlying allocation at an offset, so codegen sees an allocation whose alignment is smaller than the type it must load, violating the invariant `alloc_align >= layout.align.abi` and causing an ICE. The corrected transformation only performs this propagation when `alloc.inner().align >= op.layout.align.abi`; otherwise it falls back to copying into a properly aligned value.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR constants/operands handled by GVN where a value is obtained by transmuting (or otherwise reinterpreting bytes of) an allocation with smaller alignment into a type with larger ABI alignment, e.g. `Option<u32>` (alignment 4) transmuted to `u64` (alignment 8). Trigger requires the source allocation to be `GlobalAlloc::Memory` and be eligible for const-prop interning, and GVN enabled (e.g. `-Zmir-opt-level=0 -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN` or normal optimized builds).
analysis.trigger: A GVN-propagated constant operand points into a `GlobalAlloc::Memory` allocation whose `alloc.inner().align` is less than the operand's `op.layout.align.abi`, reached when a transmute reinterprets a lower-alignment value as a higher-alignment type.
preconditions: GVN pass is enabled (the regression test forces it via -Zmir-opt-level=0 -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN, though it is also reachable in normal optimized builds).
The constant pointer's provenance resolves to a GlobalAlloc::Memory allocation that can be interned for constprop.
The allocation's alignment is less than the ABI alignment of the operand type (e.g. None::<u32> bytes reinterpreted as u64).
The operand is eligible to be represented as ConstValue::Indirect rather than copied.
pitfalls: Propagating an allocation as Indirect is only sound if the allocation satisfies the operand type's ABI alignment; otherwise codegen's alignment assertion fails.

The GlobalAlloc::Memory check alone is insufficient; the code comment notes statics/Indirect interplay ('Codegen will choke on an `Indirect` with anything by `GlobalAlloc::Memory`'), but this fix specifically addresses alignment, not the GlobalAlloc kind.
Falling through to copying is the intended safe fallback; do not assume all memory allocations can be referenced indirectly.
Do not conflate this alignment fix with borrowing/overwrite issues or other GVN transformations; the decoded MIR diff warning notes these are separate conditions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused UI build-pass regression test under `tests/ui/mir/alignment/` (historical file `misaligned-constant-gvn.rs`) with `//@ build-pass` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-opt-level=0 -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN`, containing a transmute from a lower-aligned value to a higher-aligned type (`let variant: Option<u32> = None; let transmuted: u64 = unsafe { std::mem::transmute(variant) }; println!("{transmuted}");`). The test asserts compilation succeeds (no codegen ICE). To construct a differing pair: same program with GVN propagation forced versus a variant where the allocation alignment is sufficient, or inspect that the corrected path falls back to copying when alignment is insufficient.
evidence: Verify that allocations output by GVN are sufficiently aligned.
Transmuting a constant is just an offset in the allocation. If the alignment of the
allocation is not enough, fallback to copying into a properly aligned value.
Codegen will choke on an `Indirect` with anything
by `GlobalAlloc::Memory`, so do fall through to copying if needed.
